Hypothesis Bayes factors of a fitted model

Source: R/hypothesis-model.R
hypothesis_BF_model.Rd

hypothesis_BF_model() is the engine behind hypothesis_BF() of a BayesTools_fit, exported for packages that test hypotheses on the parameters of their own models. It parses the statements with the parameter catalog of the model, resolves each to one tested parameter, plans how it can be evaluated (the draws and the prior density of the tested quantity, the classification of its point values), checks every plan against the requested density backend, evaluates the statements in groups that share a tested quantity, and binds the results into one table in the order of the statements. What the engine needs to know about the model comes from its provider (hypothesis_provider()); the methods to evaluate a point hypothesis are the density backends (hypothesis_density_backend()).

hypothesis_BF_model(
  object,
  hypothesis,
  namespace = NULL,
  component = NULL,
  transform_scaled = FALSE,
  conditional = FALSE,
  logBF = FALSE,
  BF01 = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  density_method = NULL,
  density_control = NULL,
  n_samples = 10000,
  columns = "default",
  parameter = NULL,
  conditional_omitted = FALSE
)

Arguments

object

a model object with a hypothesis_provider() method.

hypothesis

character vector with hypothesis statements (see hypothesis_BF()). Names of the parameter catalog of the model need no backticks. The statements of a model are character strings: a parsed hypothesis (hypothesis_parse()) stops with an error of class BayesTools_hypothesis_statement.

namespace

the component of the model the statements refer to, in the vocabulary of its provider (for a BayesTools_fit: "auto", the formula parameters such as "mu", "model", or "random"); NULL selects the default.

component

a catalog component (the level token of a factor term) passed to hypothesis_resolve(): a reference to a factor term without a level stands for this level, so that "x_fac = 0.1" with component = "B" is the statement "x_fac[B] = 0.1". It combines with namespace, which selects the formula parameter (for example when the factor is shared by several formulas).

transform_scaled

whether coefficients of scaled predictors, and random-effect SDs, variances, and correlations of such predictors, are tested on the original scale (TRUE) or on the fitted scale (FALSE, the default), as in JAGS_estimates_table().

conditional

whether to test each quantity conditionally on its inclusion event: spike-and-slab and mixture coefficients through as_mixed_posteriors() (conditional parameter, rule "AND"), random-effect quantities through parameter_mixed_posterior(). Without it a point null on a quantity with a prior point mass at that value stops with BayesTools_point_mass_at_null; region hypotheses are tested.

logBF, BF01, seed, columns

see hypothesis_BF().

density_method

the name of a registered density backend (hypothesis_density_backends()); matching ignores case and accepts an unambiguous partial name. NULL selects the first backend of the provider (the stored method of a marginal-means provider).

density_control

the settings of the density backend (a named list that the backend validates), or NULL.

n_samples

the number of prior samples or grid points for the deterministic marginal prior densities and for the prior draws of random-effect quantities.

parameter

for a marginal-means provider, the marginal-means parameter that the statements refer to.

conditional_omitted

whether the caller omitted conditional; the engine then warns when the full ensemble of a mixture prior is tested (full_ensemble() of the provider).

Value

A BayesTools_hypothesis_BF table, as returned by hypothesis_BF(), with the rows labelled as the statements were written. When an ordinate backend computed ordinates, the table can carry the density_diagnostics attribute of the backend.

Details

Every statement is planned before any is evaluated: the plan records the tested target (its weights on the fitted coefficients, its prior density and declared atoms), the classification of each point value by prior_ordinate_status(), and what refuses it. A statement that the requested density backend cannot evaluate stops with its refusal before anything is computed. The refusals are classed conditions; callers match the class and never the message:

BayesTools_hypothesis_statement

a statement that has to be restated, or an argument that has to change: point expressions that are no direct reference (for example "2 * mu = 0"), nonlinear expressions of factor levels, one quantity named by several names, and references that BayesTools refuses (BayesTools_parameter_resolution_error, for example BayesTools_parameter_not_found for an unknown name or level, which keeps its fields alias and available). BayesTools_hypothesis_ambiguous (parent BayesTools_hypothesis_statement) marks a statement whose references still name several model parameters, and BayesTools_hypothesis_component_mismatch a statement whose parameters belong to another component than the requested one; BayesTools_hypothesis_parameter_mismatch a marginal-means statement that refers to another parameter than parameter.

BayesTools_hypothesis_unavailable

a test that cannot be computed, with the more specific BayesTools_hypothesis_fixed (the quantity is fixed by the fitted model), BayesTools_hypothesis_target (no supported target or prior density), or BayesTools_hypothesis_method (the density backend is unavailable for the target). A point hypothesis whose prior ordinate is not exact, finite, and regular stops with the class of prior_ordinate_status() (for example BayesTools_point_mass_at_null) and BayesTools_hypothesis_ordinate.

A density backend owns its own conditions (a failed ordinate, a model it does not support).

Random numbers: the draws of every statement are extracted while it is planned, without seed; seed only reaches the evaluation of the Bayes factors of the draws (hypothesis_BF()) and the prior draws of random-effect quantities that have no prior density.
